findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] AuthenticatorUtils (package authenticators.util) now statically imports AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator (package authenticators.browser) while AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator simultaneously imports AuthenticatorUtils, creating a browser↔util package cycle. Anyone reorganizing the browser authenticators package or splitting these modules later hits a compile-time tangle; the constant USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH now has two reasons to move and each move breaks the other side. A better home for setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError is the browser package itself (or a shared constants class), which would delete the import in one direction.

[BUG] UsernameForm.authenticate() calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but no such no-arg method exists in UsernameForm, AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator, or anywhere in this diff — and UsernameForm has no webauthnAuth field to implement it from. The changed line cannot compile as diffed; either the helper is added in a hunk not shown (making this diff incomplete/self-inconsistent) or UsernameForm breaks the build for every browser-flow deployment, not just passkey users.

[ADVISORY] The authenticate() path now gates webauthnAuth.fillContextForm() on isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) which requires user != null, so the initial-login page (user not yet identified) no longer gets webauthn form data set in authenticate(); the only remaining fill site is the challenge(context, error, field) overload, which is not the path used by the formData challenge on first render. On the very first login page with conditional passkeys enabled, the webauthn conditional-UI form attributes may never be populated, silently disabling autofilling passkeys at initial login; the new tests only assert the webauthn form after the user is identified or in a different flow, so this regression would ship unverified.

[ADVISORY] The new setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError() re-auth form handling (USERNAME_HIDDEN, REGISTRATION_DISABLED) is exercised by no assertion in any test — PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey checks the error message and webauthn form presence after a wrong password but never asserts the username field is hidden or registration disabled on that error page. A regression in this path (e.g. the auth note not propagated, or form attributes dropped) would render a re-auth error page that leaks/requires the username field for an already-identified user, and no test in the diff would fail.

[ADVISORY] reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey() verifies webauthn absence with a try { assertThat(element, nullValue()); fail(...) } catch (Exception) block instead of Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...), which only passes when findElement throws and reports the confusing message 'Not expected to have webauthn button' on failure. The assertion is inverted and fragile: if the element is found, assertThat throws AssertionError which is not caught by catch (Exception) so the fail() message is never the one shown; the next maintainer editing this test gets misleading diagnostics and the pattern invites copy-paste into future tests.

[ADVISORY] webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey() deletes the events.clear() that previously ran after logout(), so the first expectLogin() assertion can match a stale login event from before the current webauthn login. The passkey-login assertion becomes vacuous — it passes even if the clickAuthenticate() login silently fails and the appPage check is satisfied by residual state — weakening the only verification that the external-key passkey re-auth flow actually produces the expected login event.

[BUG] Moving the fillContextForm call under isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) removes WebAuthn form setup on the initial (first-factor) username/password page when no user is set, regressing conditional-UI (autofill) login for flows that use UsernamePasswordForm. Previously, webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) ran when webauthnAuth != null && isPasskeysEnabled() even with context.getUser() == null, initializing conditional-UI data on the first login page; the new guard requires user != null, so on a fresh login via the username+password form the page no longer carries the WebAuthn conditional-UI attributes and the browser passkey autofill never triggers — a first-login regression not traceable to the stated re-authentication intent.

[ADVISORY] The util-package class now reads the browser-package constant AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH (and the visibility was widened from protected to public solely for this), inverting the package layering between util and browser. Maintainers of the browser authenticators can no longer refactor or rename the auth-note constant without breaking a package that conceptually sits below them; every future shared auth-note helper will follow this precedent and the util/browser boundary erodes, making the next change to re-authentication notes harder and riskier.

[ADVISORY] badPasswordHandler now unconditionally calls AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context), hoisting a browser-forms concern (USERNAME_HIDDEN / REGISTRATION_DISABLED form attributes) into the shared util method, so the constant-widening plus util extraction is pure relocation with no behavioral addition over the deleted inline block. The extraction adds a new public util API and a cross-package dependency while the three removed lines are the only caller behavior change is null; a future reader auditing re-auth form behavior must now trace through two packages to find the same three attribute sets, increasing change risk without deleting any branches or lines net.

[ADVISORY] The diff flips the organization-flow assertion from 'webauthn form absent after username selected' to 'webauthn form present', a deliberate behavior change for users without a discoverable credential that is asserted in a test but not traceable to any requirement in the re-authentication PR description. Organization users with only a non-discoverable WebAuthn key now see a passkey form on the password page after selecting username; if this is unintended UI exposure for the org flow, the shipped behavior differs from the stated intent, and the test now locks in whichever behavior shipped rather than the requirement.

[BUG] The challenge() error path inverts the old user-null condition: previously webauthn data was filled exactly when context.getUser() == null, now fillContextForm is skipped for the fresh-login error case because isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null. A user on an initial (non-re-auth) login whose context.getUser() is null when the challenge is re-rendered (e.g. a failed credential attempt before the user is bound to the context) loses the passkey/conditional-UI form entirely after a typo, leaving password-only recovery where the old code kept the passkey option; no test in the diff covers webauthn form presence on a first-login error with user unset.

[BUG] The webauthn setup moved out of the user==null branch in authenticate() and is now gated on user != null, so on a fresh login (no user identified yet) fillContextForm is no longer invoked from authenticate(), inverting the prior behavior where conditional-UI setup happened precisely when the user was not selected. The initial username/password page for a passkeys-enabled realm no longer gets the WebAuthn conditional-UI attribute set from this call site; the fresh-login passkey autofill only survives if some other uncovered call site (the formData challenge overload) fills it, and any regression there is invisible to the diff's tests which only assert webauthn form presence at fresh login in one scenario.

[ADVISORY] isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) conflates two orthogonal conditions — 'the passkeys feature/policy is enabled' and 'the user has been identified' — under a name that only describes the first, and its logic is duplicated in a differently-shaped no-arg variant in UsernameForm. The next change to passkeys gating (e.g. a per-user passkey-availability check, or a policy flag rename) must be applied in two hand-maintained variants that already disagree on their parameter shape; a future editor updating one and not the other silently splits the login vs re-auth behavior. Extracting the 'user identified && passkeys enabled' predicate into a shared single-source (e.g. AuthenticatorUtils next to setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError) deletes the duplication.

[ADVISORY] setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError is bound to the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH auth-note sentinel via stringly-typed Boolean.parseBoolean of an auth note that no code path in this diff writes, widening the constant to public to reach it. The re-auth form-shaping behavior depends on an auth note set by a call site outside this diff; if any re-auth entry path (e.g. a custom flow or IdentityProvider re-auth) fails to set that note, the error form silently renders as a full login form with username editable and registration enabled, exposing registration UI during re-authentication. A typed helper that both sets and reads the note would make the invariant single-sourced.

[ADVISORY] The UsernameForm skip condition now consults a realm-wide passkeys flag instead of the user's actual credentials, so re-authenticating users who have no passkey at all still get the username form where the PR's stated intent was only to let passkey users re-authenticate. Any realm with the passkeys policy flag enabled loses the long-standing re-auth optimization for every user (broker-linked or not, passkey holder or not): a password-only user re-authenticating with prompt=login is forced through an extra username-form page even though their identity is fully known — this is a silent objective change from 'enable passkeys at re-auth' to 'show username form to everyone in passkeys-enabled realms', codified without explicit human sign-off by the reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey test which asserts the form appears instead of the previous skip-to-password behavior.

[ADVISORY] This test's assertions were inverted mid-review to expect the webauthn form on the username/password page where the original test explicitly asserted its absence (Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException...)), flipping a previously-verified behavior guarantee rather than adding a new case. The prior tested intent — 'username/password page for a user with a non-discoverable key shows no webauthn form because the conditional-UI mediation for that user already finished' — was silently replaced with the opposite expectation via a one-line assertion flip, so any downstream consumer relying on the old page shape (custom themes checking for the absent webauthn form) sees the change shipped as part of an unrelated 're-authentication with passkeys' fix with no acceptance record of the behavioral reversal.

[ADVISORY] setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError decides 're-authentication' solely from the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH auth note, whereas the previous inline code in AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler consulted isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth(context), which can also consider the live context user; any flow that sets the user in the AuthSession context without writing that note now renders the re-auth challenge with USERNAME_HIDDEN unset, so the username field becomes editable mid-re-authentication. During a prompt=login (or max_age) re-authentication driven by a flow that pre-populates the user without the auth note, a failed password attempt renders a fully editable username+password form; an attacker at an unlocked browser (or an XSS-adjacent session) can pivot the re-auth prompt into a fresh login as a different account, defeating the 'authenticate the same user again' contract the re-auth flow promises.

[ADVISORY] UsernameForm.authenticate now skips the user-set shortcut whenever passkeys are enabled, unconditionally invoking the username form during re-authentication, and the isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() call reads realm policy without any per-user credential check, so the presented form's security posture depends on the WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators()==false override to avoid leaking a re-auth user's registered authenticator list via fillContextForm. If a custom deployment swaps WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator for the base WebAuthnAuthenticator in the conditional-passkeys flow, the base class's shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators (user != null) returns true during re-auth and fillContextForm enumerates the victim user's registered WebAuthn credential list (labels/AAGUIDs) to the login page, giving an unauthenticated observer fingerprinting info that was previously only shown post-identification.

[BUG] The diff inverts the condition for filling webauthn data on the initial username/password page from `context.getUser() == null` (anonymous, pre-selection) to `user != null` (post-selection), and no test in this diff asserts the presence or absence of the webauth conditional-UI form on the anonymous first page of the UsernamePasswordForm flow. If fillContextForm on the anonymous page is needed for the browser's conditional-mediation autofill to trigger before the user types a username, that regression ships undetected: PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey types the username and checks the webauth form only after the user is already selected (and the Organization test was updated to the new post-selection expectation), so the no-user path has zero coverage. Test files checked: PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java, PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java, PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.java.

[ADVISORY] The new setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError behavior (setting USERNAME_HIDDEN and REGISTRATION_DISABLED on the error form during re-auth) is never asserted by any test in the diff — the closest test, webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey, checks only the webauth form element and the error text after a bad password, never that the username field is actually hidden or registration link suppressed. A regression that re-displays the editable username field on the re-auth error page (e.g. the auth note key renamed or the attribute lost in challenge()) passes the entire new test suite, leaving users able to switch identity mid re-authentication.

[ADVISORY] The UsernameForm behavior change — no longer skipping the form when the user is already set, if conditional passkeys are enabled — has no test in this diff that exercises the UsernameForm flow (both new webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication tests run the UsernamePasswordForm flow with the execution switched to UsernamePasswordFormFactory.PROVIDER_ID). The new branch in UsernameForm.authenticate (user set + passkeys enabled → show form instead of context.success()) is verified by no modified test; realms using the plain UsernameForm authenticator with passkeys enabled get a behavior change (extra username step during re-auth) that nothing in CI would catch if broken either way.

[ADVISORY] The reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey test wraps `assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue())` inside `try { ... fail(...) } catch (Exception nsee)`, a pattern where the assertion only fails via the uncaught AssertionError path and the catch swallows every RuntimeException from findElement indiscriminately. The check reads as asserting absence but actually passes on any driver exception (stale element, timeout, WebDriver errors), so an intermittent Selenium failure during that block is silently interpreted as 'webauthn button correctly absent', producing a false-green on exactly the assertion meant to prove passkeys are not shown.

[ADVISORY] The test named reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey actually disables passkeys realm-wide via setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE), so the scenario its name claims (passkeys enabled but this user has no passkey credential) is never tested. The user-without-passkey-but-realm-passkeys-on case — which exercises the new isConditionalPasskeysEnabled path with a user that has no webauthn credentials — remains uncovered; the test's comment ('Passkeys login should not be available on the page as this user does not have passkey') misleads future maintainers into thinking that branch is verified.

goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

Since `findElement` throws `NoSuchElementException` when absent, the success path relies on an exception, and if the element is present the `assertThat(..., nullValue())` fails with `AssertionError` (not caught by `catch (Exception)`), so the custom `fail()` message is never used. This is a real, diff-grounded test fragility/diagnostics issue, not a product behavior defect.

This aligns with production changes that now keep/prepare passkeys UI when a user is already identified (e.g., UsernamePasswordForm now calls `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` i.e., `user != null`, and WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator adjusts what authenticators are shown). adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(context, String error, String field)`, the old logic populated passkeys/webauthn UI data specifically when `context.getUser() == null` (`if (context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()) { webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context); }`). The diff replaces this with `if (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()))` where `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` explicitly requires `user != null`. This is a real behavioral change: any error re-render where the user is still not bound to the context (e.g., bad/unknown username or other paths leaving `context.getUser()` null) will no longer call `fillContextForm`, so the conditional passkeys UI data won’t be set on the error page even though it previously was. The added/updated tests assert webauthn presence mainly when the user is already identified, and do not cover the user-null error rerender case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The webauthn setup moved out of the user==null branch in authenticate() and is now gated on user != null, so on a fresh login (no user identified yet) fillContextForm is no longer invoked from authenticate(), inverting the prior behavior where conditional-UI setup happened precisely when the user was not selected. The initial username/password page for a passkeys-enabled realm no longer gets the WebAuthn conditional-UI attribute set from this call site; the fresh-login passkey autofill only survives if some other uncovered call site (the formData challenge overload) fills it, and any regression there is invisible to the diff's tests which only assert webauthn form presence at fresh login in one scenario.

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably changes UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate() from calling webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) whenever passkeys are enabled to calling it only when isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) is true, and that helper explicitly requires user != null (new method at bottom of UsernamePasswordForm). The same user!=null gating is also applied in the error challenge path. This means on an initial username+password screen where context.getUser() is not yet identified, this call site no longer populates any WebAuthn/conditional-UI form state via fillContextForm, reversing the previous behavior at this location. Whether another call path still sets up the conditional UI isn’t shown in the diff, so this is a plausible functional regression introduced by the change itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) conflates two orthogonal conditions — 'the passkeys feature/policy is enabled' and 'the user has been identified' — under a name that only describes the first, and its logic is duplicated in a differently-shaped no-arg variant in UsernameForm. The next change to passkeys gating (e.g. a per-user passkey-availability check, or a policy flag rename) must be applied in two hand-maintained variants that already disagree on their parameter shape; a future editor updating one and not the other silently splits the login vs re-auth behavior. Extracting the 'user identified && passkeys enabled' predicate into a shared single-source (e.g. AuthenticatorUtils next to setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError) deletes the duplication.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` which returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`, i.e., it mixes “passkeys enabled” with “user identified” under a name that reads like only the former. Separately, `UsernameForm.authenticate()` is changed to gate on `context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`, implying another passkeys-gating predicate exists/gets used there with a different shape (no-arg) than the new `UserModel`-arg predicate. While the exact duplication can’t be fully confirmed without seeing `UsernameForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`’s implementation, the diff does show passkeys gating logic now exists in at least two places/classes and could drift, making this a concrete maintainability/architecture concern rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError is bound to the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH auth-note sentinel via stringly-typed Boolean.parseBoolean of an auth note that no code path in this diff writes, widening the constant to public to reach it. The re-auth form-shaping behavior depends on an auth note set by a call site outside this diff; if any re-auth entry path (e.g. a custom flow or IdentityProvider re-auth) fails to set that note, the error form silently renders as a full login form with username editable and registration enabled, exposing registration UI during re-authentication. A typed helper that both sets and reads the note would make the invariant single-sourced.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)` which reads `context.getAuthenticationSession().getAuthNote(USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH)` and gates behavior via `Boolean.parseBoolean(...)`. In this diff, there is no corresponding code that *sets* that auth-note; instead, the constant is widened from `protected` to `public` in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` so it can be referenced from `AuthenticatorUtils` (via static import). That creates a cross-class invariant dependent on some external call site not shown here, and keeps the re-auth form-shaping logic “stringly-typed” and split between writer (elsewhere) and reader (new util). Whether this becomes a runtime bug cannot be verified from the diff alone, but the coupling/robustness concern is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The UsernameForm skip condition now consults a realm-wide passkeys flag instead of the user's actual credentials, so re-authenticating users who have no passkey at all still get the username form where the PR's stated intent was only to let passkey users re-authenticate. Any realm with the passkeys policy flag enabled loses the long-standing re-auth optimization for every user (broker-linked or not, passkey holder or not): a password-only user re-authenticating with prompt=login is forced through an extra username-form page even though their identity is fully known — this is a silent objective change from 'enable passkeys at re-auth' to 'show username form to everyone in passkeys-enabled realms', codified without explicit human sign-off by the reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey test which asserts the form appears instead of the previous skip-to-password behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a broad behavior change in `UsernameForm.authenticate`: it no longer skips the username step for re-authentication when `context.getUser() != null` if `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is true (`if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) { ... context.success(); }`). That means in passkeys/conditional-UI-enabled scenarios, even a fully-identified reauth user will be forced through the username form in flows that use `UsernameForm`, which is a UX/flow optimization regression concern grounded in the diff. However, the finding overreaches in two ways that are not verifiable from this diff: (1) it asserts `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is purely realm-wide and ignores user credentials (the method body isn’t shown here), and (2) it claims the new `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` test “asserts the [username] form appears” — that test is in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest` (single combined form) and only checks that the WebAuthn form is not shown when realm passkeys are disabled, not that the username step is introduced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] This test's assertions were inverted mid-review to expect the webauthn form on the username/password page where the original test explicitly asserted its absence (Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException...)), flipping a previously-verified behavior guarantee rather than adding a new case. The prior tested intent — 'username/password page for a user with a non-discoverable key shows no webauthn form because the conditional-UI mediation for that user already finished' — was silently replaced with the opposite expectation via a one-line assertion flip, so any downstream consumer relying on the old page shape (custom themes checking for the absent webauthn form) sees the change shipped as part of an unrelated 're-authentication with passkeys' fix with no acceptance record of the behavioral reversal.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does flip existing test expectations in `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest#passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey` from asserting the WebAuthn form is absent (`Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException...)`) to asserting it is present (`driver.findElement(...), notNullValue()`). That inversion aligns with the production change in `UsernamePasswordForm`, which now calls `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` (i.e., user != null) instead of only when `context.getUser() == null`, thereby changing the page shape for the username/password screen after a user is identified. Whether this behavior change is desired is not provably a defect from the diff alone, but it is a concrete, potentially breaking UI/contract change beyond just adding a new re-authentication case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError decides 're-authentication' solely from the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH auth note, whereas the previous inline code in AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler consulted isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth(context), which can also consider the live context user; any flow that sets the user in the AuthSession context without writing that note now renders the re-auth challenge with USERNAME_HIDDEN unset, so the username field becomes editable mid-re-authentication. During a prompt=login (or max_age) re-authentication driven by a flow that pre-populates the user without the auth note, a failed password attempt renders a fully editable username+password form; an attacker at an unlocked browser (or an XSS-adjacent session) can pivot the re-auth prompt into a fresh login as a different account, defeating the 'authenticate the same user again' contract the re-auth flow promises.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler()` no longer calls `isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth(context)` and instead always delegates to `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)`, which *only* checks the auth note `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` (via `context.getAuthenticationSession().getAuthNote(...)`) to decide whether to set `LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN`/`REGISTRATION_DISABLED`. If `isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth` previously also considered other state (e.g., `context.getUser()`), that broader behavior would be lost. However, the implementation of `isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth` is not shown in this diff, so it’s not verifiable from the provided changes that a real security/correctness regression definitely exists—only that the decision logic is now explicitly note-based.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] UsernameForm.authenticate now skips the user-set shortcut whenever passkeys are enabled, unconditionally invoking the username form during re-authentication, and the isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() call reads realm policy without any per-user credential check, so the presented form's security posture depends on the WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators()==false override to avoid leaking a re-auth user's registered authenticator list via fillContextForm. If a custom deployment swaps WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator for the base WebAuthnAuthenticator in the conditional-passkeys flow, the base class's shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators (user != null) returns true during re-auth and fillContextForm enumerates the victim user's registered WebAuthn credential list (labels/AAGUIDs) to the login page, giving an unauthenticated observer fingerprinting info that was previously only shown post-identification.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show `UsernameForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` implementation, so claims about it “reading realm policy without any per-user credential check” and “unconditionally invoking the username form during re-authentication whenever passkeys are enabled” are not verifiable from the provided changes. Additionally, the PR explicitly adds `WebAuthnAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` and overrides it in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` to return `false`, which directly prevents listing authenticators in the conditional-passkeys authenticator. The remaining concern relies on a hypothetical custom deployment swapping authenticators, which is speculative and not a defect demonstrated by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The diff inverts the condition for filling webauthn data on the initial username/password page from `context.getUser() == null` (anonymous, pre-selection) to `user != null` (post-selection), and no test in this diff asserts the presence or absence of the webauth conditional-UI form on the anonymous first page of the UsernamePasswordForm flow. If fillContextForm on the anonymous page is needed for the browser's conditional-mediation autofill to trigger before the user types a username, that regression ships undetected: PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey types the username and checks the webauth form only after the user is already selected (and the Organization test was updated to the new post-selection expectation), so the no-user path has zero coverage. Test files checked: PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java, PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java, PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.java.

adjudication.rationale: The finding’s core claim that “the no-user path has zero coverage” is contradicted by the diff: PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithExternalKey() asserts the presence of //form[@id='webauth'] immediately after opening the login form (before any username is entered), and PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey() also asserts the webauth form exists before submitting the username. So the anonymous/initial-page presence of the WebAuthn conditional-UI form is in fact asserted in this diff. While UsernamePasswordForm does change when it calls webauthnAuth.fillContextForm (now gated by isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) which requires user != null), the specific allegation that this regression would “ship undetected” due to lack of tests is not supported by the shown tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError behavior (setting USERNAME_HIDDEN and REGISTRATION_DISABLED on the error form during re-auth) is never asserted by any test in the diff — the closest test, webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey, checks only the webauth form element and the error text after a bad password, never that the username field is actually hidden or registration link suppressed. A regression that re-displays the editable username field on the re-auth error page (e.g. the auth note key renamed or the attribute lost in challenge()) passes the entire new test suite, leaving users able to switch identity mid re-authentication.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces nontrivial new behavior in `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(...)` that sets `LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN` and `LoginFormsProvider.REGISTRATION_DISABLED` when the auth note `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` is true (moved/centralized from `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler` and also invoked from `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse`). The added/modified tests (e.g., `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey`, `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`, and others) assert presence/absence of the WebAuthn form and error/info messages, but none assert that the username field is hidden/non-editable or that registration is disabled on the re-authentication error page. Therefore, a regression in propagating that auth note or in applying these form attributes would not be caught by the new tests. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap, not a verifiable functional defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The UsernameForm behavior change — no longer skipping the form when the user is already set, if conditional passkeys are enabled — has no test in this diff that exercises the UsernameForm flow (both new webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication tests run the UsernamePasswordForm flow with the execution switched to UsernamePasswordFormFactory.PROVIDER_ID). The new branch in UsernameForm.authenticate (user set + passkeys enabled → show form instead of context.success()) is verified by no modified test; realms using the plain UsernameForm authenticator with passkeys enabled get a behavior change (extra username step during re-auth) that nothing in CI would catch if broken either way.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new logic in `UsernameForm.authenticate` to *not* short-circuit when `context.getUser() != null` if conditional passkeys are enabled (`if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) { ... context.success(); }`). None of the modified/added tests in this diff explicitly assert the UsernameForm re-authentication behavior (i.e., whether the UsernameForm is shown vs skipped when the user is already set and passkeys are enabled). The new tests focus on successful passkey re-authentication outcomes, but they don’t validate that this specific UsernameForm branch is exercised/correct, so a regression in that behavior could slip through without CI detection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey test wraps `assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue())` inside `try { ... fail(...) } catch (Exception nsee)`, a pattern where the assertion only fails via the uncaught AssertionError path and the catch swallows every RuntimeException from findElement indiscriminately. The check reads as asserting absence but actually passes on any driver exception (stale element, timeout, WebDriver errors), so an intermittent Selenium failure during that block is silently interpreted as 'webauthn button correctly absent', producing a false-green on exactly the assertion meant to prove passkeys are not shown.

[ADVISORY] The test named reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey actually disables passkeys realm-wide via setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE), so the scenario its name claims (passkeys enabled but this user has no passkey credential) is never tested. The user-without-passkey-but-realm-passkeys-on case — which exercises the new isConditionalPasskeysEnabled path with a user that has no webauthn credentials — remains uncovered; the test's comment ('Passkeys login should not be available on the page as this user does not have passkey') misleads future maintainers into thinking that branch is verified.

adjudication.rationale: The new test `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest` explicitly disables realm passkeys via `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)`, so it cannot exercise the new `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)` path (which requires `webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` and `user != null`). This makes the test name/comment misleading (it claims "user has no passkey" as the reason passkeys UI is absent, but the diff shows the realm-level flag is what prevents passkeys). As a result, the scenario where realm passkeys are enabled but the identified user lacks WebAuthn credentials is not covered by this test.
